proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matching ordinary and supplied-channel homogeneity-testing frontiers, with saturation, explicit finite tests, likelihood-mixture lower bounds, and consistency criteria. Mathematical and decision panels passed after source attestation; the field novelty claim failed because the strict benchmark has limited reach and upper-separation constants leave vast finite-resource ranges vacuous. The independent validity check confirmed incremental novelty, so the run stopped before Lean formalization; a broader-class theorem would require a re-anchored topic.
tldr: For the prospective maintained binary hidden-treatment benchmark, the original-record minimax homogeneity separation has matched order \(\min\{1,(n\eta^4)^{-2/5}\}\). Supplying the true channels on the same model gives matched order \(\min\{1,(n\eta^2)^{-2/5}\}\). The ordinary radius tends to zero exactly when \(n\eta^4\to\infty\), and the supplied radius tends to zero exactly when \(n\eta^2\to\infty\); under these respective conditions explicit tests are also uniformly consistent at every fixed nonempty separation. Total finite tests have full-constant-null finite-sample size control, and positive original-record likelihood mixtures prove the matching converses for every randomized test. No logarithmic factor occurs. The results quantify the cost of distinguishing causal effect variation from diagnostic reliability variation within this prospective benchmark; the matched upper bounds do not extend to the full published hidden-treatment class.
